I’ve witnessed the end of days.

scene wakanaastrip1
And through it all, of course I’ve had my fair share of problems.
In fact, there have been so many problems that it would take me a whole cycle just to recount them.
But I’ve not been without support.
Throughout this entire journey, there’s been someone right beside me the whole time.
Someone who has kept me grounded, and knows me better than almost anyone.
That someone is this desk.
: I love you, desk.
: (Is a desk)
Unfortunately, some things in life just aren’t fair. And the things we want to speak to the most completely ignore us.
But that’s okay. Because sometimes, other things or creatures show up to keep us company.
: Come in.
scene wakanaastrip2
: Did I just hear you...tell your desk that you love it?
And sometimes they call you out on things you’d really wish they didn’t hear and weren’t actually able to call you out on.
: No.
: Arakawa.
: What?
: Do you want to fuck your desk?
: I don’t want to fuck my desk, Wakana. I was just recalling how long it’s been with me and how much we’ve been through together.
: Oh my god. You want to fuck your desk.
: Wakana, why are you here?
scene wakanaastrip3
: I came to ask if you’d like to accompany me out to the city if you didn’t have any plans tonight. But seeing as you do and they involve fucking your desk, I will just wait until tomorrow.
: You know, this is exactly why I never speak when no one’s around. Someone always shows up exactly when they’re not supposed to.
: Yes, I apologize for interrupting your...confession. I will take my leave now.
: Wait, no. You don’t have to go.
: I’m aware. I wasn’t actually planning on leaving. I just wanted to make it seem as if I was so you’d have less of a desire to fuck your desk and-
: Wakana, why are you inviting me to the city? Are Osako and Imani busy?
scene wakanaastrip4
: No. I’d just rather go with you instead.
: Right. And what’s the catch, exactly?
: Can the catch be that you don’t slam me up against another wall and act all tough? That wasn’t particularly enjoyable for me last time. I’m sure it’s a precious memory for you, though.
: I promise not to slam you up against anything. But I still don’t get why it has to be me instead of one of them.
: You really want to fuck that desk, don’t you?
: I don’t want to fuck the desk, Wakana.
: Arakawa, despite me not owing you an explanation for literally anything ever, I’m asking you to come with me because you are my friend and I value you as a person.
: Do you value me as a coworker as well?
: Absolutely fucking not. You should have been fired years ago.
: This is going to be a really fun trip, isn’t it?
: We shall see when we arrive at our destination.
: And that destination is?
scene black
: A secret. Now, come. Unless you need a moment to say goodbye to the desk.
: Please don’t make this a thing.
: It is far too late for that, I’m afraid.
Despite having thirty minutes left of my “counseling” session, I decide to leave early so Wakana can reap whatever benefits of our friendship she’s after today.

Unfortunately for me, I highly doubt one of those benefits will be my penis. So I will remain blissfully ignorant for the next hour or so as she drags me to an unknown location to not have sex with me.
scene noonsky
It becomes evident that by “the city,” Wakana literally meant the city as we get off the train at the first stop in the urban district.
With most people getting out of work around this time, navigating through the station becomes a chore.
But, as if she’s an expert when it comes to this exact pathway, Wakana quickly guides me to the nearest exit and the two of us make our way out into the street.
It’s nice out today, but it’s also not.
I like that I get to be here with her, but I also don’t.
I’m conflicted in a number of ways and long for the one who has always been there for me.
scene wakanaastrip5
My beautiful desk.
scene wakanaastrip6
Just kidding.
As it turns out, the “secret” place Wakana wanted to bring me was a third location of that same bookstore I’ve gone to with Futaba in the past.
You know, the one she tried to confess her feelings for me in.
Or the one we were kicked out of during the second Dorm Wars for...huh. Why were we kicked out again?
Either way, I’m here now with someone else. And today’s someone is not only significantly more well-versed in the world of literature, but a better writer as well. Probably.
Come to think of it, I haven’t read or heard any of Wakana’s poetry. But I’m sure it exists since she’s always going off the rails about the art form as a whole.
Come to think of something else, there’s not really much I know about Wakana to begin with.
But her wanting me here is all I really need to know right now.
Maybe we are the kind of friends who can just “hang out” without there needing to be some sort of ulterior motive or purpose for it.
Maybe she’s believed that this whole time and I have been the weird one for expecting there to be more to it.
And maybe today will be the day I do learn more about her.
I think I’d like that.
I think I’m lonely.
: Have you figured out why we’re here yet, Arakawa?
: To hang out?
: Yes and no. We are “hanging out.” This much is true. But more than that, I need your help with something.
: Just “oh?” No snide remark or sexual innuendo in regard to what it is I need?
: Not today.
scene wakanaastrip7
: Is something the matter?
: No. Just tell me whatever it is you need help with.
: Okay. But, in doing so, I’d like to invoke the “catch” you had me add earlier and ask that you do not sexually assault me after I tell you.
: I’ll do my best.
scene wakanaastrip8
: I’m conducting some independent research on a woman who may have been close to you. And by may, I mean you were reduced to a hulking manchild the last time I brought her up in a scenario like this.
: I don’t know what you’re talking about.
: So The Girl Who Cannot Breathe rings no bells whatsoever?
: Nothing at all? Not a peep?
scene wakanaastrip9
: Hah...

: Arakawa, listen...if it makes you feel any better, I’m not doing this for you. You’re an adult and it is well within your right to keep whatever secrets you’ve bottled up over the years to yourself.
: Would I hear them out should you wish to unbottle them? Sure. But I will not force it out of you, nor belittle you for your reluctance in opening up to me.
: Then why are you doing this?
scene wakanaastrip10
: Because either your niece has a remarkable gift or she has plagiarized her work for my poetry contest and must be punished. Though, I am leaning toward the former given your background as well.
: Either way, I know you know something. And that even if you’ve given up on ever telling anyone anything about the way you’re feeling, you value your niece.
: What good will getting involved do if she has a “gift?” It’s poetry. It’s not like she needs an athletic coach or anything like that. She can just write and that’ll be it.
: A gift is not always a good thing, Arakawa. A wrong message in the right hands can change the world for the worse.
: And you think you can swoop in and prevent that from happening by...what? Finding more work from a writer you supposedly know all about already?
scene wakanaastrip11
: There would be no need for research if I already knew everything, Arakawa. But the hint that I was given at the beach was enough to prompt this investigation.
: It could be anything. A second pen name. The title of an anthology more of her work was published in. It’s like I’m trying to put together a puzzle right now and I only have half of the pieces.
: If you know something, help me. Because if your niece did write that poem, it could mean she’s following in the footsteps of someone who got lost in the dark long before you and I did.
: You’re her guardian, are you not? Isn’t it your responsibility to make sure she stays on the right path? Because she’s veering off, Arakawa. We are teachers. We must help her.
: It’s just a poem, Wakana.
scene mm1
scene mm2
scene mm3
scene mm4
scene mm5
scene wakanaastrip12
: You know damn well that nothing is “just a poem,” Arakawa! I don’t understand why you keep saying that!
: You said just the other day that “The Road Not Taken” is just a poem. Are you changing your mind already?
: That was me being biased and pretentious! So if it gets you to open your fucking eyes, yes. I am changing my mind.
: Your niece is mimicking the writing style of one of the most talented, yet utterly sickening artists to ever find their way onto my shelf.
: And yes, her work was emotionally evocative and brimming with a level of creativity few others have ever been able to match. But what she preached was madness.
: You have a responsibility. As a teacher. As a parent. As whatever the fuck you want to call yourself. And if you want to mope on your own time, have at it!
scene wakanaastrip13
: But right now, there is a girl who is on the brink of walking down a very dark path. And she needs our help.
: You got all of that from one poem?
: Arakawa...it wasn't one poem.
: She submitted twenty of them.
: And all of them could have won the competition.
: So either she really is mass plagiarizing, or there is something going on in her head that you need to be worried about. Because if her mother is who I think she is-
: Thank you for your concern.
scene wakanaastrip14
: I don’t know anything and Ami will be fine.
: There’s that look again...The same one you gave me last time. And the same one you probably would have given me if you didn’t just walk away on the beach.
: Just how much do you know about all of this?
: I told you. I don’t know anything.
: But you’re lying, Arakawa. You do.
: Even if that’s true, I wouldn’t have to tell you about it. And you should be minding your own business when it comes to my niece. There’s no need for you to get involved over a contest.
: Why did you stop writing?...
: What are you to her?...
scene black
: Nothing anymore.
I step outside while Wakana finishes conducting whatever “research” she needs to do in the bookstore.
Frankly, I don’t really care.
And I was foolish for ever hoping that I wouldn’t be needed for something today.
